answer: Neighborhood Cutoff. Each agent maintains a fixed-capacity neighbor list, and inbound service is only honored from peers reachable within two hops of that list. Newcomers can only enter by displacing an existing edge, so a fable of endless free entry fails. An attacker must seed many connected nodes and keep them mutually adjacent, paying real bandwidth and slot contention per identity. A comet of one-off accounts gets cut off at the boundary, and juniper swaps of neighbors trigger revalidation churn.
